arxiv-1904-11519.title: Multiparticle correlation studies in \Pp Pb collisions at \sqrtsNN = 8.16 \TeV
arxiv-1904-11519.description: Abstract The second- and third-order azimuthal anisotropy Fourier harmonics of charged particles produced in \Pp Pb collisions, at \sqrtsNN = 8.16 ​ \TeV \sqrtsNN=8.16\TeV , are studied over a wide range of event multiplicities. Multiparticle correlations are used to isolate global properties stemming from the collision overlap geometry.

arxiv-2101-12451.title: A Study on the Association between Maternal Childhood Trauma Exposure and Placental-fetal Stress Physiology during Pregnancy
arxiv-2101-12451.creator: Eileen Zhang
arxiv-2101-12451.description: Abstract Abstract Background It has been found that the effect of childhood trauma (CT) exposure may pass on to the next generation. Scientists have hypothesized that the association between CT exposure and placental-fetal stress physiology is the mechanism. A study was conducted to examine the hypothesis.

arxiv-2201-03964.title: A stochastic gradient descent approach with partitioned-truncated singular value decomposition for large-scale inverse problems of magnetic modulus data
arxiv-2201-03964.creator: Wenbin Li, Kangzhi Wang, Tingting Fan
arxiv-2201-03964.description: Abstract 1 Abstract We propose a stochastic gradient descent approach with partitioned-truncated singular value decomposition for large-scale inverse problems of magnetic modulus data. Motivated by a uniqueness theorem in gravity inverse problem and realizing the similarity between gravity and magnetic inverse problems, we propose to solve the level-set function modeling the volume susceptibility distribution from the nonlinear magnetic modulus data.

arxiv-2301-04883.title: SlideVQA: A Dataset for Document Visual Question Answering on Multiple Images
arxiv-2301-04883.creator: Ryota Tanaka, Kyosuke Nishida, Kosuke Nishida, Taku Hasegawa, Itsumi Saito, Kuniko Saito
arxiv-2301-04883.description: Abstract Visual question answering on document images that contain textual, visual, and layout information, called document VQA, has received much attention recently. Although many datasets have been proposed for developing document VQA systems, most of the existing datasets focus on understanding the content relationships within a single image and not across multiple images.

arxiv-2311-04141.title: Benchmarking a Neutral-Atom Quantum Computer
arxiv-2311-04141.creator: N. Wagner, C. Poole, T. M. Graham, M. Saffman
arxiv-2311-04141.description: Abstract In this study, we simulated the algorithmic performance of a small neutral atom quantum computer and compared its performance when operating with all-to-all versus nearest-neighbor connectivity. This comparison was made using a suite of algorithmic benchmarks developed by the Quantum Economic Development Consortium.

arxiv-2403-01522.title: Gender Equity in Physics Labs: A Review
arxiv-2403-01522.creator: Danny Doucette, Chandralekha Singh
arxiv-2403-01522.description: Abstract This review article provides an overview of research on the topic of gender equity in educational physics labs. As many institutions and instructors seek to evolve or transform physics lab learning, it is important that changes are made that improve equity for all students along multiple axes of identity, including gender.

arxiv-2403-08356.title: Parameter Constraints on Traversable Wormholes within Beyond Horndeski Theories through Quasi-Periodic Oscillations
arxiv-2403-08356.creator: Farukh Abdulkhamidov, Petya Nedkova, Javlon Rayimbaev, Jutta Kunz, Bobomurat Ahmedov
arxiv-2403-08356.description: Abstract Hunting compact astrophysical objects such as black holes and wormholes, as well as testing gravity theories, are important issues in relativistic astrophysics. In this sense, theoretical and observational studies of quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) observed in (micro)quasars become helpful in exploring their central object, which can be a black hole or a wormhole.

arxiv-2502-08781.title: Europe’s AI Imperative
arxiv-2502-08781.creator: Gjergji Kasneci, Urs Gasser, Thomas F. Hofmann, Gerhard Kramer, Gerhard Müller, Claudia Peus, Helmut Schönenberger, Enkelejda Kasneci
arxiv-2502-08781.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gjergji Kasneci, Urs Gasser, Thomas F. Hofmann, Gerhard Kramer, Gerhard Müller, Claudia Peus, Helmut Schönenberger, Enkelejda Kasneci. Executive Summary Europe is at a make-or-break moment in the global AI race, squeezed between the massive venture capital and tech giants in the US and China’s scale-oriented, top-down drive. At this tipping point, where the convergence of AI with complementary and synergistic technologies, like quantum computing, biotech, VR/AR, 5G/6G, robotics, advanced materials, and high-performance computing, could upend geopolitical balances, Europe needs to rethink its AI-related strategy.

arxiv-2504-18319.title: Eigenvarieties over CM fields and trianguline representations
arxiv-2504-18319.creator: Vaughan McDonald
arxiv-2504-18319.description: Abstract We show that the Galois representations associated to points on certain (derived) eigenvarieties for GL n \operatorname{GL}_{n} over a CM field are trianguline with the expected Sen weights, verifying an analogue of a conjecture of Hansen in many cases.

arxiv-2505-14530.title: Internal Chain-of-Thought: Empirical Evidence for Layer - wise Subtask Scheduling in LLMs
arxiv-2505-14530.creator: Zhipeng Yang, Junzhuo Li, Siyu Xia, Xuming Hu
arxiv-2505-14530.description: Abstract We show that large language models (LLMs) exhibit an internal chain-of-thought : they sequentially decompose and execute composite tasks layer-by-layer. Two claims ground our study: (i) distinct subtasks are learned at different network depths, and (ii) these subtasks are executed sequentially across layers.

arxiv-2508-02969.title: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent based Augmented Lagrangian Method for Constrained Nonconvex Nonlinear Optimization
arxiv-2508-02969.creator: Mingze Li 1,2 , Student Member, IEEE, Lei Fan 1,2 , Senior Member, IEEE, and Zhu Han 1 Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2508-02969.description: Abstract Nonlinear programming (NLP) plays a critical role in domains such as power energy systems, chemical engineering, communication networks, and financial engineering. However, solving large-scale, nonconvex NLP problems remains a significant challenge due to the complexity of the solution landscape and the presence of nonlinear nonconvex constraints.

arxiv-2510-27332.title: Jacobi capture as a pathway to off-center massive black hole binaries in dwarf galaxies
arxiv-2510-27332.creator: Thibaut L. François
arxiv-2510-27332.description: Abstract The recent detection of high-redshift supermassive black holes with JWST has renewed interest in the processes driving black hole growth. At the same time, both simulations and observations point to a widespread population of off-center intermediate-mass black holes in dwarf galaxies. Their ability to merge outside galactic centers may play a key role in shaping black hole mass assembly.

arxiv-2511-03528.title: Quantum effects in the magnon spectrum of 2D altermagnets via continuous similarity transformations
arxiv-2511-03528.creator: Raymond Wiedmann, Dag-Björn Hering, Vanessa Sulaiman, Matthias R. Walther, Kai P. Schmidt, Götz S. Uhrig
arxiv-2511-03528.description: Abstract We investigate quantum effects on magnon excitations in a minimal spin-1/2 Heisenberg model for 2D altermagnets on the square lattice. A continuous similarity transformation is applied in momentum space to derive an effective Hamiltonian that conserves the number of magnon excitations.

pmc-11304074.title: Comparison of the Application Value of Transthoracic Echocardiography in Diagnosing Patent Foramen Ovale Under Different States of Stimulation: A Retrospective Study
pmc-11304074.creator: Jianwei Shi, Haijuan Gu, Wenjun Fan, Jiesheng Xia, Huanhuan Gu
pmc-11304074.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate the application value of contrast‐enhanced transthoracic echocardiography (cTEE) in the diagnosis of patent foramen ovale (PFO) under different states of stimulation, with the goal of enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of PFO diagnosis.MethodsThis research consecutively enrolled patients suspected of having PFO from October 2022 to February 2024, presenting primary clinical symptoms such as unexplained syncope, headache, dizziness, and stroke.

pmc-11358989.title: An Integrated Navigation Method Aided by Position Correction Model and Velocity Model for AUVs
pmc-11358989.creator: Pengfei Lv, Junyi Lv, Zhichao Hong, Lixin Xu
pmc-11358989.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). When autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) perform underwater tasks, the absence of GPS position assistance can lead to a decrease in the accuracy of traditional navigation systems, such as the extended Kalman filter (EKF), due to the accumulation of errors. To enhance the navigation accuracy of AUVs in the absence of position assistance, this paper proposes an innovative navigation method that integrates a position correction model and a velocity model.

pmc-11435567.title: A Morphometric Study on the Dimensions of the Vertebral Canal and Intervertebral Discs from Th1 to S1 in Cats and Their Relevance for Spinal Diseases
pmc-11435567.creator: Jessica Richter, Christoph K. W. Mülling, Nicole Röhrmann
pmc-11435567.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryThe vertebral canal dimensions are crucial for spinal health, as degenerative changes can significantly affect the spinal cord. Compression of spinal nerves at the lumbosacral junction causes cauda equina syndrome (CES), more common in dogs than cats. With regard to the limited information on feline vertebral canal dimensions, this study examined 50 cats, measuring the interpedicular (ID) and midsagittal (SD) diameters as well as the intervertebral disc width (IVDW) in 28 of these animals.

pmc-11509453.title: How Encephalopathy Impacts Language Ability: A Scoping Review of the Linguistic Abilities of Adults with Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
pmc-11509453.creator: Ioanna Papatheodorou, Stavroula Stavrakaki, Vasiliki Koukoulioti, Martha Spilioti, Vasileios Kimiskidis, Allison B Reiss
pmc-11509453.description: Background and Objectives: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy refers to a group of conditions where patients experience abnormal development due to various causes as well as frequent epileptiform discharges that ultimately contribute, in an independent and additive fashion, to cognitive and linguistic impairments. The language and cognition outcome of these patients in adulthood has been understudied.

pmc-12613441.title: Rapid prognostic tools in disaster medicine: C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) and bicarbonate-to-lactate ratio (BILAR) in crush syndrome
pmc-12613441.creator: Nazmiye Serap Biçer, Mehmet Biçer, Davut Eren, Hilal Sipahioğlu, Belgin Zeybek Oral, Banu Açmaz, Sümeyra Koyuncu
pmc-12613441.description: BackgroundCrush syndrome is a life-threatening complication frequently observed following earthquakes and other natural disasters, often leading to multi-organ failure and high mortality. Rapid and reliable prognostic tools are critical for early risk stratification and management of affected patients, particularly in resource-limited disaster settings.

pmc-12654619.title: Unveiling the Role of Graphite Morphology in Ductile Iron: A 3D FEM-Based Micromechanical Framework for Damage Evolution and Mechanical Performance Prediction with Applicability to Multiphase Alloys
pmc-12654619.creator: Jing Tao, Yufei Jiang, Shuhui Xie, Yujian Wang, Ziyue Zhou, Lingxiao Fu, Chengrong Mao, Lingyu Li, Junrui Huang, Shichao Liu, Elena Pereloma
pmc-12654619.description: The mechanical performance of cast iron is strongly governed by the morphology of its graphite phase, yet establishing a quantitative link between microstructure and macroscopic properties remains a challenge. In this study, a three-dimensional finite element method (FEM)-based micromechanical framework is proposed to analyze and predict the mechanical behavior of cast iron with representative graphite morphologies, spheroidal and flake graphite.

pmc-12749258.title: Compressive sensing techniques based on secure data aggregation in WSNs
pmc-12749258.creator: Marwa E. Madkour, Salah E. Soliman, Moawad I. Dessouky, Fathi E. Abd El-Samie, Mohammed E. Hammad, Amir S. Elsafrawey
pmc-12749258.description: This research paper presents an efficient data collection scheme for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) that simultaneously compresses and encrypts sensor data to extend network lifespan. To address WSN resource limitations, the scheme combines Compressive Sensing (CS) with Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) and Elliptic Curve Diffie–Hellman (ECDH) key exchange.

pmc-13389189.title: Establishing demographic-based normative values for neurofilament light chain and glial fibrillary acidic protein in serum and plasma samples
pmc-13389189.creator: Tyler L Borko, Alanna Ritchie, Sean Selva, Stefan Sillau, Eric Engebretson, Andrew B Wolf, Enrique Alvarez, Robert Gross, Eric Gutierrez, John Corboy, Diego Silva, Ryan Kammeyer, Amanda L Piquet, Timothy L Vollmer, Salim Chahin, Gregory Owens, Jeffrey L Bennett, Kavita V Nair
pmc-13389189.description: BackgroundInterpretation of neurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) levels in blood requires reference ranges from healthy cohorts, accounting for demographic features.ObjectiveTo compare serum and plasma NfL and GFAP in healthy individuals, accounting for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI).MethodsAdolescents through older adults were recruited at Colorado community events and a senior clinic.

pmc-13425850.title: Recurrent Peritoneal Inclusion Cyst With Persistent Pelvic Pain Despite Radiologic Improvement: A Management Challenge
pmc-13425850.creator: Kiran Javaid, Riana Tarabocchia, Maria Balabanian, Omar Bellorin-Marin, Rory Ulloque, Rahul Mittal
pmc-13425850.description: Peritoneal inclusion cysts (PICs) are benign cystic lesions that most commonly occur in women with a history of prior abdominal surgery, endometriosis, or pelvic inflammatory disease. They arise from the accumulation of peritoneal fluid within adhesions and are associated with high recurrence rates despite available treatment options.

pmc-13601256.title: Preparedness of CT technicians and radiographers for severe contrast media reactions: knowledge gaps and training needs
pmc-13601256.creator: Haneen E. Abuanzeh, Ayman M. Al-Qaaneh
pmc-13601256.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSevere contrast media reactions during computed tomography (CT) are rare but potentially life-threatening and require rapid recognition and coordinated emergency response. CT technicians and radiographers are often frontline professionals during contrast-enhanced CT, yet their preparedness in Jordan remains underexplored.ObjectiveTo assess knowledge of severe contrast media reactions among CT technicians and radiographers in Jordan and identify factors associated with total knowledge scores.MethodsA descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using an online questionnaire adapted from a previously published tool.
